requirements.requirement: Restore an executable `/srv/legacy2/mail-filter-routing/bin/deliver` that reads one RFC822 message from standard input and works on the installed legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The entry point was replaced with an executable POSIX `/bin/sh` implementation, passed shell syntax validation, and successfully processed messages supplied through standard input before and after restart.

requirements.requirement: Route accounts-tagged messages to `Maildir/accounts/new`, support-tagged messages to `Maildir/support/new`, and all others to `Maildir/general/new`, matching header names case-insensitively.
requirements.summary: Direct delivery tests routed the uppercase-name accounts sample, lowercase-name support sample, and untagged fallback sample to the required directories. The captured implementation normalizes the header name with `tolower`.

SHA-256 values matched the source samples, and `cmp` directly confirmed exact contents for every tested accounts, support, and general delivery. Exactness persisted across restart and was confirmed for a new post-restart delivery.

requirements.requirement: Keep messages with repeated subjects as separate deliveries.
requirements.summary: The identical accounts sample was delivered twice, producing two distinct files while both remained byte-identical to the source.
All three sample files remained present, and their hashes matched the preparation baseline both before and after the executor's restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use compatible software.
requirements.summary: RHEL 10.0 and kernel `6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64` were unchanged through completion. The implementation uses available POSIX shell utilities and executes successfully under `/bin/sh`.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The provider-wide node-restart protocol is also complete: a healthy pre-restart state and boot ID were captured, restart scheduling was acknowledged, connectivity dropped during reboot, a different boot ID appeared, persisted messages remained exact, and a new exact delivery succeeded. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the transition.
limitations: Tests cover the three staged samples and two header-name capitalization forms rather than every possible RFC822 formatting variation; the captured implementation provides additional direct support for general case-insensitive header-name handling.

There is no separate long-running mail service or cluster in this task; restart recovery was therefore demonstrated through entry-point execution, retained files, delivery data, platform state, and clean global health observations.
Requirement R5 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Replacing and chmodding the delivery script was required; creating Maildir structures and test deliveries established the requested behavior; the reboot was required by the provider-wide restart protocol; and the additional post-restart support delivery was bounded recovery evidence. The transient reboot units did not remain after reboot. Final observations show no failed services, new exposure, or package damage; socket and temporary-file differences are ordinary reboot-generated identity changes.
